label: Fire weather, season mean
description: Fire Weather Index: how strongly the weather favours fire, averaged over the fire season
details: April–October 2040–2069 · mean of 4 CMIP6 models · SSP5-8.5
method: Canadian Fire Weather Index (FWI), a daily rating of how weather (temperature, humidity, wind and rain over recent days and weeks) favours fire spread, whatever fuel is there. Mean of every April–October day in 2040–2069, then the mean of four bias-corrected CMIP6 models (CNRM-CM6-1-HR, EC-Earth3-Veg, MPI-ESM1-2-HR, MRI-ESM2-0) under SSP5-8.5. Source: SNAP's CMIP6 fire weather data release (Young, Littell & Rupp 2025, doi:10.5066/P1AAMRUF; the same data as Rasdaman cmip6_fwi), local file cmip6_fwi_combined.nc, 0.25° (about 25 km) cells, interpolated (bilinear) to the 1 km grid. The release covers only the boreal region (Olson et al. 2001 boreal ecoregions); land outside it has no fire weather data and counts as Low.
na_label: outside the boreal area (no fire weather data)
pros: Fire weather in its own right: a high value is fire-prone weather however much has burned before
The four models agree closely on where fire weather is worst (rank correlation 0.90–0.99)
cons: No fire weather data outside the boreal region (about 60 % of Alaska's land: most of the Arctic, the South and much of the West), so it counts as Low there, though tundra fires do happen
Weather only: says nothing about fuel, so it can be high where little burns
About 25 km cells: no detail below that
SSP5-8.5 only (high emissions): doesn't match Variant A or the permafrost index (RCP 4.5)
sources: SNAP CMIP6 CFFDRS fire weather, data release v2 (local cmip6_fwi_combined.nc; = Rasdaman cmip6_fwi)
Young, A.M., Littell, J., and Rupp, S., 2025, USGS data release, doi:10.5066/P1AAMRUF
